title: Psalms Chapter 143 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 143 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 143 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 143.

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalm 143?
questions.explanation: Psalm 143 is explicitly identified as 'A Psalm of David' in Psalms 143:1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:2, why should the LORD not enter into judgment with His servant?
options: Because no man living shall be justified in His sight
questions.correctAnswer: Because no man living shall be justified in His sight
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:2 states: 'for in thy sight shall no man living be justified.'

questions.question: What has the enemy done to the psalmist's soul according to Psalms 143:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:3 says, 'For the enemy hath persecuted my soul.'

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his life after being smitten by the enemy in Psalms 143:3?
options: Made to dwell in the light
Made to dwell in a palace
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:3 states, 'he hath made me to dwell in darkness, as those that have been long dead.'

questions.question: What is the condition of the psalmist's spirit in Psalms 143:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:4 says, 'Therefore is my spirit overwhelmed within me.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:1, what two qualities of God does the psalmist ask to answer him in?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:1 requests God to answer in 'thy faithfulness' and 'thy righteousness.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 143:2 teaches that no man living can be justified in God's sight.
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:2 states, 'for in thy sight shall no man living be justified.'

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 143:4, the psalmist's heart is described as joyful and peaceful.
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:4 describes the heart as 'desolate,' not joyful or peaceful.

questions.question: What action does the psalmist take towards God in Psalms 143:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:6 says, 'I stretch forth my hands unto thee.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist compare his soul's thirst to in Psalms 143:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:6 states, 'my soul thirsteth after thee, as a thirsty land.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:7, what does the psalmist request the LORD not to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:7 says, 'hide not thy face from me.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 143:7 expresses concern that if God hides His face, the psalmist will be like those who go down into the pit.
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:7 says, 'lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:8, what does the psalmist trust in?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:8 states, 'for in thee do I trust.'

questions.question: What is the first request the psalmist makes in Psalms 143:1?
questions.explanation: The opening of Psalms 143:1 is 'Hear my prayer, O LORD.'

questions.question: In Psalms 143, which comes first?
options: The psalmist asks God to deliver him from enemies
The psalmist remembers the days of old
The psalmist stretches forth his hands
The psalmist asks God to enter not into judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist asks God to enter not into judgment
questions.explanation: In the sequence of the chapter, Psalms 143:2 says 'And enter not into judgment with thy servant' which comes before remembering days (v5), stretching forth hands (v6), or deliverance from enemies (v9).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 143 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 143 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:5, what does the psalmist do when he remembers the days of old?
options: He meditates on all God's works
questions.correctAnswer: He meditates on all God's works
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:5 states that the psalmist remembers the days of old and meditates on all God's works, musing on the work of His hands, showing a reflective trust in God's past faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Psalms 143:6 describe the psalmist's soul in relation to God?
options: It thirsts after God as a thirsty land
It is satisfied like a full cup
It is fearful like a frightened child
questions.correctAnswer: It thirsts after God as a thirsty land
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:6, the psalmist stretches forth his hands to God and his soul thirsts after Him as a thirsty land, illustrating a deep longing and dependence on God.

questions.question: What urgent request does the psalmist make to the LORD in Psalms 143:7?
options: Hear me speedily and hide not your face
questions.correctAnswer: Hear me speedily and hide not your face
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:7 shows the psalmist asking the LORD to hear him quickly and not to hide His face, fearing that otherwise he will be like those who go down into the pit, highlighting his urgent need for God's presence.

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:8, why does the psalmist want to hear God's lovingkindness in the morning?
options: Because in God he trusts and seeks guidance
Because he wants to glorify God publicly
Because he desires to receive material blessings
questions.correctAnswer: Because in God he trusts and seeks guidance
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:8 explains the psalmist's desire to hear God's lovingkindness in the morning as an expression of trust and a request for guidance on the right way to walk, reflecting faith and obedience.

questions.question: What does Psalms 143:10 teach us about the psalmist's attitude toward God's will?
options: The psalmist asks God to teach him to do His will
The psalmist wants to question God's will
The psalmist refuses to accept God's will
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist asks God to teach him to do His will
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:10, the psalmist humbly requests God to teach him to do His will, indicating a desire for obedience and submission to God's guidance.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his spirit in Psalms 143:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:4 describes the psalmist's spirit as overwhelmed and his heart within him as desolate, reflecting deep distress and sorrow.

questions.question: What does Psalms 143:9 reveal about the psalmist's response to enemies?
options: He flees to the LORD to hide
questions.correctAnswer: He flees to the LORD to hide
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:9, the psalmist expresses reliance on the LORD for protection, fleeing to Him to hide from enemies, demonstrating trust and humility.

questions.question: What promise is connected between Psalms 143:6 and Psalms 143:7 regarding God's response to prayer?
options: Because the soul thirsts for God, the psalmist asks God to hear him speedily
Because the psalmist is joyful, he asks God to bless him
Because the psalmist is strong, he asks God to give him enemies
Because the psalmist is silent, he asks God to punish him
questions.correctAnswer: Because the soul thirsts for God, the psalmist asks God to hear him speedily
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:6 shows the psalmist's soul thirsting for God, which leads in Psalms 143:7 to an urgent plea for God to hear him speedily and not hide His face, linking deep spiritual longing with urgent prayer.

questions.question: What does Psalms 143:8 say will happen if the psalmist trusts in God and lifts up his soul?
options: He will know the way to walk
He will be free from all troubles immediately
He will no longer need to pray
questions.correctAnswer: He will know the way to walk
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:8 teaches that trusting in God and lifting up the soul results in God causing the psalmist to know the way he should walk, emphasizing guidance through faith.

questions.question: How does Psalms 143:11 demonstrate the psalmist's view of God's righteousness?
options: He asks God to quicken him for God's righteousness' sake
questions.correctAnswer: He asks God to quicken him for God's righteousness' sake
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:11, the psalmist requests God to revive him for the sake of God's name and righteousness, showing reverence and trust in God's just character.

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:12, what does the psalmist ask God to do to those who afflict his soul?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:12 asks God, out of mercy, to cut off the psalmist's enemies and destroy all who afflict his soul, reflecting a plea for divine justice on behalf of the faithful servant.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 143:2 teaches that no man living can be justified in God's sight.
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:2 clearly states that no man living shall be justified in God's sight, emphasizing human dependence on God's mercy rather than self-righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 143:3, the enemy has only mildly troubled the psalmist’s soul.
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:3 describes severe persecution of the psalmist’s soul, being smitten down and made to dwell in darkness like the dead, indicating great distress, not mild trouble.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 143:1 emphasizes prayer with a request for God’s faithfulness and righteousness in answering.
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:1 opens with the psalmist asking the LORD to hear his prayer and answer him in faithfulness and righteousness, highlighting a trust in God’s character.

questions.question: What does Psalms 143:5 imply about the importance of remembering God's past works for present faith?
options: Remembering God's works strengthens faith and meditation
Remembering past works leads to despair
questions.correctAnswer: Remembering God's works strengthens faith and meditation
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:5 shows the psalmist remembering and meditating on God's works, which implies that recalling God's faithfulness in the past encourages present trust and spiritual reflection.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 143 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 143.

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:9, where does the psalmist flee to find protection?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:9 states, 'Deliver me, O LORD, from mine enemies: I flee unto thee to hide me,' showing the psalmist seeks refuge in God.

questions.question: In Psalms 143:10, what does the psalmist ask God to teach him?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Teach me to do thy will; for thou art my God,' indicating a desire to follow God's will faithfully.

questions.question: What characteristic of God's spirit is highlighted in Psalms 143:10?
questions.explanation: The psalmist refers to God's spirit as good: 'thy spirit is good; lead me into the land of uprightness,' showing the benevolent nature of God's guidance.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Psalms 143:11 for God to quicken the psalmist?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Quicken me, O LORD, for thy name's sake,' indicating the psalmist appeals to God's honor and reputation.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request be done to his enemies in Psalms 143:12?
options: Cut them off and destroy them
questions.correctAnswer: Cut them off and destroy them
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks, 'And of thy mercy cut off mine enemies, and destroy all them that afflict my soul,' requesting divine justice.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of fleeing to God for refuge as seen in Psalms 143:9?
questions.explanation: Psalm 91:2 says, 'I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress,' closely paralleling the theme of Psalm 143:9 where God is a refuge.

questions.question: How does Psalms 143:11 connect with the New Testament concept of being 'quickened' or made alive?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:11 speaks about the Spirit that raised Jesus making believers alive, paralleling the psalmist’s plea in Psalms 143:11 to be quickened by God.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Psalms 143:6 with the phrase 'my soul thirsteth after thee, as a thirsty land'?
questions.explanation: The psalmist uses a simile comparing the soul’s longing to a thirsty land, explicitly using 'as,' which is a hallmark of similes (Psalms 143:6).

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'quickens' in Psalms 143:11?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root חָיָה (chayah) means 'to live' or 'to make alive,' which aligns with the plea in Psalms 143:11 for God to 'quicken' or revive the psalmist.

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:12, how does the psalmist identify his relationship to God?
questions.explanation: The verse ends with 'for I am thy servant,' clearly defining the psalmist’s humble submission to God.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament reflects the theme of God leading into 'the land of uprightness' as in Psalms 143:10?
questions.explanation: John 14:6 states Jesus is 'the way, the truth, and the life,' corresponding to God leading the psalmist into uprightness (Psalms 143:10).

questions.question: What does the psalmist fear will happen if God hides His face, according to Psalms 143:7?
options: He will be like those who go down into the pit
questions.correctAnswer: He will be like those who go down into the pit
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:7 says, 'hide not thy face from me, lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit,' indicating fear of death or destruction without God's presence.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 143:8 shows the psalmist trusts in God and seeks guidance on the way to walk.
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk,' demonstrating trust and desire for divine guidance.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 143:2 states that some men living can be justified in God's sight.
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:2 says, 'for in thy sight shall no man living be justified,' denying justification for any living man before God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 143:5 reflect the psalmist's contemplation?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands,' showing reflection on God’s deeds.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 143 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 143 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 143:1 reveal about the nature of prayer?
options: It is a request for help
It is a form of worship
It is a way to command God
questions.correctAnswer: It is a request for help
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:1 shows that prayer is a cry for assistance: 'Hear my prayer, O LORD, give ear to my supplications.' This suggests a dependence on God for help, indicating prayer’s role as a request for divine aid.

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:2, what is the condition of humanity before God?
options: Humans are justified by their actions
No man living can be justified
questions.correctAnswer: No man living can be justified
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:2 states, 'for in thy sight shall no man living be justified,' emphasizing humanity's inability to achieve righteousness before God on their own, highlighting the necessity of grace.

questions.question: What metaphor does David use in Psalms 143:3 to describe his suffering?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:3, David indicates that his enemy has caused him to 'dwell in darkness, as those that have been long dead,' symbolizing deep despair and hopelessness.

questions.question: What emotional state does David express in Psalms 143:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:4 reveals David's emotional turmoil: 'Therefore is my spirit overwhelmed within me,' highlighting his distress and need for God's intervention.

questions.question: How does David seek God's presence in Psalms 143:6?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:6, David's act of stretching forth his hands symbolizes his longing for God: 'I stretch forth my hands unto thee: my soul thirsteth after thee,' indicating deep spiritual yearning.

questions.question: What does David request in Psalms 143:8 regarding his spiritual direction?
options: To know the way he should walk
To be delivered from his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: To know the way he should walk
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:8, David asks God to 'cause me to know the way wherein I should walk,' demonstrating his desire for divine guidance in his life.

questions.question: What is a significant theme in Psalms 143:9 regarding David's enemies?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:9, David states, 'Deliver me, O LORD, from mine enemies,' indicating his reliance on God for rescue from those who oppress him.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 143:10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:10 mentions, 'thy spirit is good,' which emphasizes God's goodness as a guiding force in David's life, reflecting His benevolent nature.

questions.question: According to Psalms 143:11, why does David ask God to quicken him?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:11, David requests, 'Quicken me, O LORD, for thy name's sake,' indicating that he desires revival not just for personal benefit, but to honor God's reputation.

questions.question: What does Psalms 143:12 teach about God's mercy?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:12 shows David asking God to 'cut off mine enemies' by His mercy, demonstrating the potency of God's mercy to protect and deliver His servants.

questions.question: How does Psalms 143:5 connect to the theme of remembrance?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:5, David reflects, 'I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works,' suggesting that reflecting on God's past deeds inspires hope and faith.

questions.question: What does David express by saying his soul thirsteth after God in Psalms 143:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:6 indicates David's deep spiritual longing: 'my soul thirsteth after thee, as a thirsty land,' which metaphorically shows his need for God’s presence and guidance.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'my heart within me is desolate' in Psalms 143:4 imply about David's condition?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:4's phrase 'my heart within me is desolate' suggests a profound sense of abandonment and despair, reflecting David's emotional struggles.

questions.question: What does Psalms 143:7 convey about David's urgency in prayer?
options: He pleads for a quick response
questions.correctAnswer: He pleads for a quick response
questions.explanation: In Psalms 143:7, David states, 'Hear me speedily, O LORD: my spirit faileth,' emphasizing his urgent need for God's immediate attention and help.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not listen to prayers. What does Psalms 143:1-2 actually teach?
questions.explanation: Psalms 143:1 states, 'Hear my prayer, O LORD,' indicating that God is attentive to the prayers of His people, directly countering the sceptics' claim of His indifference.
